gaps.sentence: They managed ___ the fire before it spread.
gaps.explanation: manage takes the to-infinitive: managed to put out.

gaps.sentence: You'd better ___ a taxi or you'll miss the plane.
gaps.explanation: had better takes the bare infinitive: you'd better take.

gaps.sentence: I'm sorry for ___ so long to reply.
He's not used to ___ so early.
gaps.explanation: be used TO + -ing: not used to getting (it's a habit he isn't accustomed to).

gaps.sentence: If you keep ___ like this, you'll exhaust yourself.
gaps.explanation: keep (+ on) is followed by -ing: keep working.

gaps.sentence: They can't help ___ at his impression of the boss.
gaps.explanation: can't help + -ing = can't stop yourself: can't help laughing.

gaps.sentence: They accused me of ___ the rules.
I want you ___ the truth, whatever it is.
gaps.explanation: want + object + to-infinitive: want you to tell.
